# Portfolio Pruning Update

Report 096 | Published 2022-10-30 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2022-10-30/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/096.json)

Portfolio rotation and consensus tradeoffs.

The prior short-term rally and slower hiking pace were supported, while the 2023 recession call failed. Rising federal interest expense and mortgage lock-in were strong structural observations. The medium-bank preference missed a funding-risk vulnerability and compares poorly with large banks in the disclosed sensitivity, even though Truist maintained its dividend. BLDR grew cash-generating capacity but did not beat the sold homebuilder comparators in that interval. Ethereum concentration concerns need role-specific denominators; Stratum software capability should not be mistaken for deployment. The RTX/eBay five-year and physical-value decade theses remain genuinely open.

**Coverage:** All article text blocks were read. Ledger covers material macro, investment, and causal propositions; incidental descriptive statistics, boilerplate, and unreasoned position lists are excluded. Image labels were read, not image pixels.

- [Proof-of-stake attack and defense](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/consensus-mechanisms/pos/attack-and-defense/) | Ethereum | Verified in the audit

Finalized blocks are not automatically reorganized; weak-subjectivity checkpoints defend newly joining nodes against long-range attacks. Social recovery and economic penalties are separate defense layers.
